study.question: Does retaining latent context/history product polarity improve click AUC beyond a magnitude-only product at identical coordinate magnitudes, parameters and normalization, and does this contrast interact with auxiliary context transfer? Observation: g0-r0039-context_product reaches0.668457307891 versus sum0.664563151244; blocked product/sum reach0.667854872059/0.667598407575. The operator-by-transfer difference-in-differences is0.003637692163, but there is only one seed and no authorized candidate diagnostics. The positive result does not yet distinguish polarity from magnitude-only multiplicative gating.
study.hypothesis: At the same learned state, signed product preserves sample-dependent agreement/opposition between tanh context queries and tanh compressed-history projections that absolute product discards. This information may improve task-conditioned readout and the direction of auxiliary context learning. The simpler magnitude-only replacement may instead regularize unreliable latent polarity and improve validation AUC; it is the new candidate, not a presumed winner. If signed product wins in both gate cells and its advantage is larger with context transfer enabled, the result supports polarity usefulness and a transfer interaction for this implementation, subject to repetitions. Magnitude-only parity or improvement rejects necessity of polarity here; neither outcome proves or refutes all multiplicative models.

study.proposed_difference: Define q=tanh(W_context*c), h=tanh(W_history*z) in FP32 as inherited; signed fusion is u=q*h and magnitude fusion u=abs(q*h). Both then use u/sqrt(mean(u^2)+1e-4), the same rank16 output map and existing history gate. For identical q,h, normalized magnitude equals abs(normalized signed), including zeros, and all coordinate magnitudes/RMS values match. This removes polarity without replacing multiplicative magnitude gating, denominator coupling or history information. Cross product polarity with existing block_aux_adapter_context_grad false/true. Submit four standalone modules: magnitude_transfer (candidate), magnitude_blocked, signed_transfer_replay and signed_blocked_replay (controls). Replays are exact historical source bytes and use the frozen seed; they measure reproducibility/runtime drift, not new independent support.
